title: KV palettization and deferred-unlock orchestrator for reduced fragmentation and prefill noise
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: high fragmentation of KV cache pages and duplicated prefill traffic cause periodic decode stalls and tail latency spikes. Root causes observed in production: small, short-lived allocations (micro-fragments) that block contiguous kernel-friendly placement, and repeated prefix-prefill for similar requests from multiple tenants. Proposal: implement a two-part runtime subsystem: (1) KV palettization: align and coalesce micro-allocations into fixed 'palettes' (micro-block groups) to reduce fragmentation and enable kernel co-placement; (2) Deferred-unlock orchestrator: replace immediate slot free with a lease + background consolidator that batches unlocks and supports lightweight migration to adjacent palettes. Add a prefill-echo suppression layer to deduplicate concurrent prefill work for overlapping prefixes. Goals: reduce 99th decode latency by 25% on tail-heavy workloads, reduce eviction churn by 30%, and improve usable KV density by ~12% across mixed-tenant traces.
technical_notes: Palettization: group allocations into 256B micro-blocks; maintain per-shard palette bitmaps for fast first-fit. Optimize for common token-span sizes observed in telemetry (8-64 tokens).

Lease-based deferred unlock: allocations return a short lease (default 150ms) instead of immediate free; explicit reclamation triggers when low memory or lease expiry. A background consolidator opportunistically migrates live fragments into contiguous palettes using a short-lived decoder-owned copy path to avoid blocking hot decode lanes.

Kernel-hint retirement: when moving fragments, annotate palettes with preferred kernel profiles (compact vs wide) so kernel selector prefers co-located fragments for low-overhead fused kernels. Update kernel selection table to consider palette density metric in addition to architecture/hw hints.

Prefill-echo suppression: maintain ephemeral prefix-inflight registry keyed by hash(prefix, model, route). If a prefill is in-flight, subsequent requests attach a lightweight waiter and reuse the computed KV fragments rather than spawning duplicate prefill work.
Telemetry: new metrics: palette_fill_ratio, deferred_unlock_rate, prefill_dedups, consolidation_migrations, palette_kernel_preference_hits. Add tag dimensions for tenancy and model_family.
Safety: leases are advisory; in emergency low-memory we will trigger synchronous reclamation (current behavior) as fail-safe to maintain correctness.
Performance budget: background consolidator must not consume >10% of a shard's decode cycles when no headroom; use token-budgeted worker threads to cap impact.
Compatibility: design allows opt-in via per-tenant config. Default rollout to internal staging only until performance gates validated.
implementation_plan: 1) Simulation: extend existing KV simulator with palette allocator and deferred-unlock behavior; run on last 30 days of production traces to estimate benefits (2 days).
2) Telemetry: add palette metrics to runtime and staging dashboards (1 day).
3) Runtime prototype: implement palette allocator and lease-based free in a feature flag gated path; add prefill-inflight registry (2 weeks).
4) Kernel selector changes: add palette_density input and preference scoring, expose kernel preference tags on palettes (3 days).
5) Background consolidator: implement token-budgeted migrator with safety checks and mem-pressure short-circuit (1 week).
6) End-to-end canary: roll to a single dedicated GPU pool with synthetic tail-heavy workload then shadow on small % of hosted requests (1 week).
7) Validation & rollback plan: write gating tests, ensure synchronous fallback to current allocator if metrics regress; prepare incident runbook (2 days).
8) Gradual rollout to remaining capacity and per-tenant opt-in for 4 weeks with active monitoring.
acceptance_criteria: Sim: >10% improvement in palette_fill_ratio and >20% reduction in eviction_count on representative traces.
Staging canary: 99th latency reduction >=15% for tail-heavy synthetic traffic and no regression in p50/p95.
Prefill deduping reduces duplicate prefill work by >=40% for common prefixes in shadowed production traces.
Background consolidator CPU token usage capped as expected (<10%).
No correctness regressions (all model outputs unchanged within existing noise bounds).
Telemetry coverage present and alerting thresholds configured for unexpected rise in reclaim events or migration failures.
alternatives_considered: Immediate compaction on free: simpler but causes decode stalls and increases tail latency — rejected due to production incidents (see incident-2025-01-12).
Coarser-grained static buckets: reduces fragmentation but wastes memory for common small allocations; palettization is more space-efficient for mixed-span workloads.

Aggressive per-request prefill coalescing at the API gateway: would reduce duplicate prefill but requires cross-tenant coordination and introduces higher coupling; decided to implement local in-runtime prefill-echo suppression first.
risks: Background consolidator could contend with decode kernels causing small latency regressions — mitigated via token-budgeting and safety limits.
Lease heuristics tuned poorly might increase short-term memory pressure and trigger excessive evictions — mitigate with conservative default lease (150ms) and dynamic adjustment based on occupancy.
Kernel selector coupling increases complexity of rollout; ensure rollback path that ignores palette hints to restore previous kernel selection behavior.
Prefill-inflight registry adds memory/CPU overhead; track prefill_dedups to ensure net saving outweighs cost.
